messages:
lee: heads-up — ap-southeast1 provisioning is backing off, a bunch of GPU attach jobs are stuck. I see local NVMe iops long-tail on the new gnode cohort.
sam: ugh. observed attach latencies ~15-90s and many retries, right? any disk errors in dmesg?
maria: saw `I/O error, dev nvme0n1` on 3 hosts. attaching logs now.
lee: paste of truncated dmesg:
```
[ 1234.567890] nvme nvme0: I/O 0xabc123 timed out
[ 1234.568012] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
[ 1235.670001] kernel: nvme_core: Completing admin command with status: timeout
```
kyle: running `iostat -x 1 5` shows %util bunched at 99.9 on nvme0n1 but rwq-sz looks normal. suspect deep GC or firmware background scrub.
sam: is this the new 7.68 drivers + fresh firmware we rolled last week? we rolled ap-southeast on Tuesday.
maria: yes firmware v7.1.2 applied Tue midnight UTC. we have a small cohort w/ refreshed drives.
lee: interesting — attach backlog correlates with scrub window starting at 00:30 local => background scrub + heavy batch provisioning probably created write amplification.
oncall: ops-bot alerted: "GPU_PROVISIONING_HOLD ap-southeast1: 42 pending" at 1719802400
kyle: quick mitigation: can we throttle janitor/scrub tasks on that cohort and move new GPU jobs to a healthy pool? control plane supports `--exclude-pool` flag for autoscaler.
maria: will open a hot patch to disable scrub on the affected nodes for 30m. prepping k8s taint plan: taint node=nvme-longtail:NoSchedule and migrate pending pods.
sam: note: moving too many jobs will spike cross-region egress cost if it spills to us-west. ops wants cost estimate before broad spill.
lee: cost wise, short-term spill is cheaper than SLA breaches. but we should target minimal spill: move only on the 12 failing hosts.
kyle: patch pushed to maintenance job to set `scrub.enabled=false` for label cohort=ap-southeaste-7. rolling now.
maria: scrub disabled on 12 hosts. starting node cordon -> drain for pending attaches. small pause, will report.
lee: drains started. attach succeed rate up to 80% now. a few hosts still show intermittent read errors, marking for proactive replacement.
oncall: filing incident ticket INC-2026-1347 and scheduling drive replacement for flagged hosts. tagging storage team.
sam: follow-up action items: 1) add telemetry to detect firmware-scrub overlap with gpu-provisioner events; 2) add auto-deprioritize scrub during heavy attach windows; 3) run firmware cohort health sweep.
maria: +1 on telemetry. I'll add a Grafana panel combining NVMe %util, kernel I/O errs, and GPU-provisioner pending counts.
kyle: logging note: we should surface `nvme-core` admin timeouts as an SLI for local-disk health.
lee: thanks team. short-term: replace 3 drives, keep 9 in monitored pool after scrub re-enable in 2 hours. long-term: ops to evaluate firmware rollouts with stagger + scrub schedule.
maria: closing loop — re-enable scrub on cohort in 2h with slower concurrency. :thumbsup:
sam: great work. adding postmortem bullets to storage runbook.
ops-bot: deploy job gpu-autoscaler-v2 started with exclude-pool flag (cohort: ap-southeast-new-nvme) at 1719803000
lee: leaving final note: cost tradeoff accepted for SLA. will sync tomorrow on firmware rollout cadence. :coffee:
